feedback: Approve for this race. The candidate changes one controller value from the best raced design (iteration 3, score 287.1): kp goes from 3.0 to 2.6, with kd 0.45, ki 0.1, base_speed 1.2, the ±0.07 m five-sensor span, sensor_size 0.016 and the weights all held fixed. The single-variable change is the right test. In iteration 3, steering_oscillation was 0.287 on the oval and 0.276 on the s-bend, both above the 0.2 level, while the slalom was 0.10. Line_loss_events fell to 0.05 on the oval and 0.0 on the s-bend and slalom, so the widened span addressed the line loss. The main open problem is off-track endings: 0 finishes on the s-bend and slalom, and max_error of 0.0625 on the s-bend, just past the 0.06 m limit. The candidate is valid: all sensor positions are inside ±0.08 m and y is in range, sensor_size 0.016 is allowed, and the weights and line_loss are allowed. Nothing in it is obviously broken. Its risk is that a lower kp weakens correction on the tightest bends, so max_error may rise. I cannot say how it will perform. Early exploration with 7 iterations left favours racing a clean one-variable test over another reading-only round. Next race, read the results as follows. If steering_oscillation is below 0.2 on the oval and s-bend and max_error is below 0.06, keep kp near 2.6 and raise base_speed in 0.1 steps (1.3, then 1.4) to test completion_time under 3 s. If oscillation is still above 0.2 at kp 2.6, raise kd toward 0.6 before changing kp again. If max_error grows above 0.065 on the s-bend while oscillation falls, kp has become too soft, so move back toward 2.8 and test sensor y position or sensor_size 0.012 for the off-track endings.
requested_changes: If steering_oscillation stays above 0.2 on the oval or s-bend at kp 2.6 with kd 0.45, raise kd from 0.45 toward 0.6 and keep kp at 2.6 (iteration 3 at kp 3.0 gave oscillation of 0.287 on the oval and 0.276 on the s-bend).

If the run is clean (steering_oscillation under 0.2, line_loss_events near 0, max_error under 0.06 on all tracks), raise base_speed in 0.1 steps to 1.3, then 1.4, with kp 2.6 and kd 0.45 held fixed, to test completion_time under 3 s (iteration 1 reached progress 0.37 on the oval at base_speed 1.4).

If max_error on the s-bend rises above 0.065 at kp 2.6 while oscillation falls, return kp to about 2.8 and test sensor y position (for example y at 0.03 m) or sensor_size 0.012 to address the off-track endings (iteration 3 max_error was 0.0625 on the s-bend, and 0 s-bend finishes).
